title: Q1 2026 Perf Baseline Suite Rollout Retrospective (Baselines + Gating)
author: Talia Benson
body:
## Purpose
This page captures the post-rollout retrospective for the Q1 2026 performance baseline + representative workload suite initiative. The rollout included:
- Defining representative traffic shapes and a locked workload suite
- Executing baseline runs across top-served models/hardware/regions
- Publishing dashboards and baseline artifacts
- Rolling out perf regression gates (warn-only → soft fail) for runtime changes

This retro focuses on what went well/poorly in baseline execution and gating rollout, and lists prioritized action items for Q2 2026.

---

## Scope and outcomes (Q1 2026)
### What shipped
1) **Baseline suite v1**
- Canonical traffic shapes with warm/cold cache modes and streaming/non-streaming variants
- Standard metric definitions (TTFT, TPOT, end-to-end latency, throughput, error rate)
- Versioned baseline artifacts (configs, seeds, prompts/prompt templates, runtime build + CUDA/driver stamping)

2) **Benchmark execution + artifacts**
- Multi-region runner with environment pinning (partial; see gaps)
- Nightly scheduled runs in perf-canary with summary diffs posted to Slack

3) **Dashboards/alerts**
- Grafana dashboards with dimensions: model, region, hardware SKU, traffic shape
- Warn-only drift alerts and links to run metadata + commit SHA

4) **Gating rollout**
- CI “perf smoke” job (non-blocking) for key microbenchmarks
- Release-train qualification updated to require a baseline suite run for runtime release candidates

### Success criteria assessment
- **Reproducible baselines:** Mostly met. p50/p95 stabilized; p99 still noisy in specific regions/SKUs and in long-context streaming.
- **Explainability:** Improved. Scheduler metrics added materially reduced time-to-triage for tail regressions.
- **Actionability for releases:** Met at “warn-only/soft fail” stage; not ready for universal hard-fail gating due to environment drift + variance pockets.
- **Operational ownership:** Improved, but oncall/runbook maturity needs work before broadening gates.

---

## Participants
Facilitator: Talia Benson (Program Management)

Core contributors (representative):
- Runtime: Mateo Alvarez, Noah Patel, Hiro Tanaka, Sofia Ivanova, Marcus Reed, Omar El-Sayed, Julian Moore
- Applied ML perf/evals: Jonas Weber, Claire Dubois, Sana Farid
- SRE/Observability: Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant, Aisha Bello, Sergio Costa
- Telemetry/Analytics: Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman
- Release Engineering: Connor O'Brien, Sahana Iyer
- Console/Dashboards: Chloe Martin, Felix Schneider

---

## What went well
### 1) Clear metric definitions and instrumentation alignment
- The project forced convergence on **TTFT/TPOT definitions**, especially for streaming, and drove fixes to first-chunk timestamp edge cases.
- Adding scheduler metrics (queue wait histograms, batch composition counters, backpressure events) materially improved confidence when attributing regressions.

Impact:
- Reduced “unknown regression” cases; most anomalies could be classified as kernel/scheduler/fleet/telemetry within 1–2 iterations.

### 2) Workload taxonomy mapped well to real production patterns (without storing sensitive prompts)
- The traffic-shape taxonomy (prompt length distributions, concurrency regimes, cache-hit scenarios) produced workloads that matched common customer issues (streaming chat, bursty concurrency, long-context).
- The approach of using **synthetic prompts + aggregated distribution shapes** made it easier to share internally and expand coverage without confidentiality risk.

### 3) Baselines became a shared language across Runtime, SRE, Release Eng, and Product
- Release qualification conversations shifted from “it seems slower” to “TTFT p95 moved by X% under shape Y on SKU Z, outside variance budget.”
- Support and customer-facing teams benefited indirectly via faster reproduction of reported latency/throughput changes.

### 4) Dashboard UX and run metadata links sped up triage
- Linking dashboard panels directly to run artifacts (config hash, seeds, runtime SHA, driver/CUDA) reduced time spent reconstructing run context.
- Observability’s early involvement prevented a worst-case scenario of unusable dashboards due to missing dimensions.

---

## What didn’t go well (and why)
### 1) Environment drift caused false positives and eroded trust early
Symptoms:
- A severe nightly regression was flagged and later attributed to **driver/CUDA mismatch** and mixed fleet composition in one region.

Root causes:
- Incomplete enforcement of environment pinning across all runners.
- Fleet normalization rules existed but were not systematically applied at scheduling time.

Impact:
- Alert fatigue risk for oncall and skepticism toward p99 deltas.

### 2) p99 variance remained high for specific shapes (especially long-context streaming)
Symptoms:
- High variance in p99 TTFT/TPOT under long-context streaming and bursty concurrency.

Root causes:
- Kernel autotune nondeterminism and caching warmup sensitivity.
- Region-level fleet heterogeneity and intermittent neighbor-noise.
- Insufficient run counts for the noisiest shapes early in the quarter (variance budget doc was still converging).

Impact:
- Limited confidence in converting certain gates from warn-only to blocking.

### 3) Gating policy operational details were under-specified for “soft fail” scenarios
Symptoms:
- Unclear guidance on when to rerun vs when to file an exception vs when to rollback.
- Teams disagreed on whether microbench regressions should block if macro baselines were flat (and vice versa).

Root causes:
- Policy existed, but exception workflow + required evidence weren’t consistently documented and practiced.

Impact:
- Release Engineering had to intervene more than desired; runtime teams occasionally bypassed signals to hit timelines.

### 4) Metrics cardinality and cost were a constant pressure
Symptoms:
- Requests for extra dimensions (tenant, route, prompt bucket, cache state) increased the risk of cardinality blowups.

Root causes:
- We tried to make dashboards serve both “deep diagnosis” and “broad health monitoring” with the same metric series.

Impact:
- Slower iteration on dashboards; increased coordination overhead with Telemetry/Analytics.

---

## Notable incidents / learnings
1) **Nightly baseline false regression due to fleet mismatch**
- Detection worked; triage was slow because environment enforcement wasn’t strict.
- Learning: “environment validity” must be a first-class check before evaluating perf deltas.

2) **Long-context streaming regression (Run 1 anomaly)**
- Baseline suite successfully isolated the shape; runtime scheduler changes (fairness/load-shedding) improved tails.
- Learning: the suite is effective when the workload shape is precise; invest in better long-context streaming representativeness.

3) **TTFT instrumentation mismatch between client and server**
- Telemetry validation harness found and fixed a streaming first-chunk timestamp issue.
- Learning: baseline metrics need periodic correctness audits, not just performance audits.

---

## Decisions made during the retro
1) **No broad hard-fail perf gates in Q2** until environment drift + variance budgets are demonstrably under control for baseline-critical shapes.
2) **Baseline validity checks are required** (driver/CUDA/runtime build + SKU constraints) before any drift evaluation.
3) **Two-tier dashboarding**
- Tier A (low-cardinality, always-on): model/region/SKU/shape summary
- Tier B (debug drilldown, sampled): cache state annotations, batch composition breakdowns, representative traces

---

## Action items (Q2 2026)
Priority key: P0 (must do), P1 (should do), P2 (nice to have)

| Priority | Action item | Owner(s) | Due | Notes / acceptance criteria |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | Enforce runner environment validity gate | Vanessa Ortiz, Sahana Iyer | 2026-05-10 | Runner must refuse to publish results if driver/CUDA/runtime build metadata doesn’t match the expected matrix; publish “invalid run” artifacts separately. |
| P0 | Introduce fleet normalization constraints at scheduling time | Vanessa Ortiz, Sean Gallagher | 2026-05-24 | For baseline runs, require homogeneous SKU pools and pinned AMI/driver; document allowable variance. |
| P0 | Finalize variance budgets per traffic shape (incl. required N trials) and encode into tooling | Sana Farid, Jonas Weber, Kira Volkov | 2026-05-31 | Tool must compute “within variance budget” vs “actionable regression” based on configured confidence intervals. |
| P0 | Gate semantics and exception workflow v2 | Connor O'Brien, Sean Gallagher, Mateo Alvarez | 2026-06-07 | Single page checklist: rerun rules, evidence required for exception, required sign-offs, and rollback triggers. |
| P1 | Expand long-context streaming shapes (cache warmup model + first-token chunking realism) | Claire Dubois, Omar El-Sayed | 2026-06-14 | Workload suite update with documented rationale; validate representativeness with Applied ML + Runtime sign-off. |
| P1 | Reduce kernel autotune nondeterminism for baseline-critical kernels | Yuki Sato, Hiro Tanaka | 2026-06-21 | Demonstrate reduced run-to-run jitter on baseline SKUs; publish before/after stability report. |
| P1 | Dashboard split into Tier A vs Tier B (cardinality controls + sampling) | Allison Grant, Sergio Costa, Felix Schneider | 2026-06-28 | Tier A always-on; Tier B behind drilldown and/or sampled traces/labels; confirm cost impact is acceptable. |
| P1 | Add automated “baseline run health” panel and alert routing rules | Aisha Bello, Sean Gallagher | 2026-06-28 | Alerts distinguish run failure vs perf drift vs invalid environment; paging only for run health failures and severe drifts on Tier A shapes. |
| P2 | Customer-facing benchmark readiness checklist (internal) | Henry Cho, Paula Mendes, Quentin Harris | 2026-07-12 | Define which baselines can be externalized, required attestation steps, and redaction rules. |

---

## Follow-ups / open questions
1) **Baseline refresh policy:** how frequently to refresh baselines for fleet changes (driver upgrades, new SKUs) vs treating as a new baseline epoch.
2) **Per-model vs per-family baselines:** whether we should standardize a smaller “Tier 0” set for gating and keep broader coverage as informational.
3) **Streaming TTFT definition in mixed transport environments:** ensure definitions hold across SDKs, proxies, and regional edges.

---

## Summary
Q1 delivered meaningful cross-org alignment and a functional baseline + gating system, but early trust was impacted by environment drift and p99 variance in a few critical regimes. Q2 priority is to harden validity enforcement, fleet normalization, and variance-aware gating semantics so perf gates can safely progress toward broader blocking use without generating noise or operational burden.
